quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When you are following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, add extra space in front of your vehicle. Do not brake suddenly. Slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid a collision.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic, you should:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let other vehicles move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, check for vehicles beside and behind you. Make sure the lane you want to enter is clear before you move.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep driving at your normal speed.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you to be alert. Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: How do you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Look at your rearview mirror often to see where traffic is behind you.

questions.question: When driving in very foggy conditions, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights to use with low beams.

questions.question: If you are already in an intersection when the green light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Continue and safely clear the intersection.
Speed up to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue and safely clear the intersection.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through and leave the intersection as quickly and safely as possible.

questions.question: When is it legal to block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered when the light was green.
During rush hour traffic.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can completely cross it before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: You want to park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: When parking facing downhill, turn your wheels toward the road edge so your vehicle rolls away from traffic if brakes fail. When parking uphill on a road with a curb, turn wheels toward the center so the vehicle rolls into the curb.

questions.question: If you must park in an unusual location, you should:

options.text: Keep your reverse lights on.
Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
questions.explanation: Park where your vehicle is visible to drivers coming from any direction. Your parked vehicle should not create a hazard.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Traffic signal ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels, so you lose steering control.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels, so you lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock your front wheels. This makes you lose steering control. To avoid hard braking, drive at a safe speed for the conditions.

questions.question: In poor weather, drivers should:

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Keep their normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when driving in bad weather. Speed limits apply only to ideal conditions.

questions.question: Alcohol at any level is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your nervous system and body functions. It reduces your judgment and focus.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean:

options.text: Passing is allowed on the left.
Passing is allowed on the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines show traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass from either direction.

questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Don't assume other drivers will let you go. Give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: A single broken white line on a highway means:

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You can cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes several times quickly.
Slow down gradually without braking.
Press the brake pedal as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without braking.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Take your foot off the gas. Do not brake. Let the car slow down on its own. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull to the side when safe.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without planning.
Check for other vehicles in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without planning.
questions.explanation: Check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes. Make sure no vehicles are in your way. Always use your turn signal to warn other drivers.

questions.question: On snow or ice, you should:

options.text: Use your cruise control.
Change speed and direction slowly and carefully.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change speed and direction slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: Make speed and direction changes slowly on snow or ice. Never use cruise control on snow or ice. Your tires may lose grip and you may lose control.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Keep your headlights on low beam.
Use high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the other vehicle.
Use your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlights on low beam.
questions.explanation: Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are near. Switch to low beams when following another vehicle closely.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit when the traffic light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive through the intersection.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, cross the intersection with caution.

questions.question: You must use low beam headlights when you are within ____ of another vehicle.

options.text: 1,000 feet
500 feet
200 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 500 feet
questions.explanation: You must use low beams when within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or when following another vehicle. High beams can blind other drivers and are unsafe.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle on your right.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane, make sure you are far enough ahead. When you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to return safely.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Use only your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Place your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors because they do not show everything behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull to the side of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull to the right edge of the road and stop. On one-way streets, move toward the nearest edge.

questions.question: How can you help the driver behind you stay a safe distance away?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Drive at a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Drive at a steady speed and signal before turning, changing lanes, or slowing down. This helps the driver behind you know what you are doing and stay at a safe distance.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign means traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to let other traffic merge safely.

questions.question: As you drive faster, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: As speed increases, your vehicle needs more distance to stop. Look far ahead so you have time to safely react to dangers.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what headlights should you use?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog. High beams reflect back off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: On a multilane road, what does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: No one can pass from either direction.
Everyone can pass from either direction.
Only the side with the dashed line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only the side with the dashed line can pass.
questions.explanation: A dashed yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. When one line is dashed and one is solid, only drivers next to the dashed line can pass.
